er.title: Energy Recharge Calculator
er.intro: Runs the current rotation for {{laps}} laps in gcsim and finds the total Energy Recharge (ER%) that lets every character’s burst go off.
er.stale: The party or rotation has changed since the last calculation, so the previous result is hidden. Press “Start calculation” to recalculate.
er.oldVersion: This result was computed with gcsim {{saved}} (now {{current}}). Please recalculate.
er.errorMismatch: Even with very high ER, burst timing does not match the baseline (run ignoring energy). Bursts are shifted for a reason other than energy.
er.note:
The number in parentheses is the share of bursts (per burst) that fired without waiting at that value. Typical and Stable are measured; Certain is an estimate from when every tried burst fired, N÷(N+1).
Even at Stable, not every burst over several laps is guaranteed to fire. Use Certain if no burst may wait.
[ ] is the error (Typical/Stable: from the number of seeds / Certain: the actual value may be lower by up to this much).
er.phaseRefine: Verifying the Typical and Stable values in gcsim
er.phaseVerify: Verifying the Certain values in gcsim
er.colTypicalTitle: Enough for 70% of the bursts. A rough guide for real play
er.colStableTitle: Enough for 90% of the bursts. Occasionally a lap falls short
er.colCertainTitle: Enough for every collected burst (verified in gcsim when verification ran). Works even with the worst luck, so it comes out high
er.colCurrentTitle: Energy Recharge calculated by gcsim from the current settings (weapon, character and artifacts included). Compared with the required values: green at Certain or above, yellow at Stable or above, red if short
er.enemyParticles: Enemy particles (non-elemental particles from enemies, crystals, drops, etc.)
er.precisionNote: The Certain value is verified by running everyone at that value in gcsim and narrowed down (rough: 10% steps, precise: 1% steps; precise takes longer). With Raiden Shogun, Kujou Sara or Dori in the party, Typical and Stable are verified the same way.
er.verifyAuto: This party includes {{names}}. Their recovery depends on their own ER, so Typical and Stable are also re-run in gcsim (this takes longer).
er.coresNote: Number of cores (Workers) used (1–{{max}}, default {{def}}, saved on this device). More cores are faster but use more memory and CPU.
er.seedsNote: Random outcomes (particles etc.) are tried with this many seeds (1–{{max}}, default 10). More seeds get closer to the true value, but the time grows in proportion. The same settings and seeds give the same result.
er.burstWaitNote: When energy is short, it counts as enough if the burst can go off within this many seconds of the particles arriving (0.1 s steps, default 0 s). The longer it is, the lower the required ER. Raise it only if you can wait in actual play.
er.introAbyss: Runs the current rotation (opening + loop) for the Stygian Onslaught fight and finds the Energy Recharge that lets every burst go off. Everyone starts with 0 energy and the first burst is judged too.
er.abyssBanner: Stygian Onslaught mode: calculates with start energy 0, timed particles and the number of loops. Results are saved separately from normal mode.
er.loopsNote: The number of times the loop part runs after the opening (default {{def}}, max {{max}}). Used for both the ER calculation and the sufficiency check. More loops catch worse windows, so the required ER rises a little, but it takes longer. Stygian Onslaught times (timed particles, no-damage periods) are seconds from the start of the battle (the start of the opening).
er.firstBurstWait: The first burst may wait up to
er.firstBurstWaitNote: Everyone starts with 0 energy, so the first burst is delayed until enough particles arrive. It counts as enough if it can go off within this many seconds of its planned time (0.5 s steps, default 0.5 s). If the opening fires a burst the result is “Unreachable”, so raise it. From the second burst on, “Wait before a burst” is used.
er.timedParticlesNote: Particles that appear at a fixed time, in seconds from the start of the battle (for example when a boss shield breaks; up to {{max}}). Handled like enemy particles, as colorless particles.
er.particleLimitTimed: [Limitation] gcsim can use only one particle setting. Because there are {{n}} timed particles, only the latest one ({{seconds}} s) is used in the calculation; the other {{ignored}} are ignored.
er.particleLimitPeriodic: [Limitation] Because there are timed particles, the enemy's periodic particles are not used in the calculation (gcsim can use only one particle setting).
er.adjustTimed: {{n}} of the {{total}} timed particles cannot be passed to gcsim (gcsim can use only one particle setting), so the app adds them to the Energy timeline itself.
er.invulnerableNote: Periods when the boss takes no damage (seconds from the start of the battle; up to {{max}}). During them, energy that requires dealing damage (Favonius-type etc.) is removed and the Sacrificial skill cooldown reset does not happen.
er.waitsColCountTitle: Burst energy waits per loop (average over {{loops}} loops and the seeds tried)
er.waitsColSecondsTitle: Average wait time per wait (cooldown waits not included). "-" when there was none
er.checkColErTitle: Energy Recharge used for the check (total; adjustable in 1% steps; defaults to the current value)
er.seedsRerollTitle: Pick the seed numbers again at random (the number of seeds does not change). Use it to see whether another set of seeds gives the same result
er.timingStale: The settings changed, so the result below is from the previous settings (press the check button to update).
er.waitsTitle: Burst energy waits (loop part only; the opening is not included)
er.waitsNote: How many times, and for how long, a burst waited for energy although its cooldown was ready ({{loops}} loops; cooldown waits not included). No waits means it is enough.
er.adjustInvulnerable: There are {{n}} no-damage periods. During them, energy that requires dealing damage (Favonius-type particles, Dehya’s skill particles, Albedo C1, Klee’s 4th passive, Rosaria C4, Crane’s Cry, Moonlight, Katsuragikiri Nagamasa, Lumidouce, Traveler (Cryo) C1, Mika C4) is removed from the calculation. The Sacrificial reset stops only in the rotation display (it is not reflected in the gcsim ER runs).
er.adjustNoVerify: Because the timeline is adjusted, the final check in gcsim is not run (a “calculation only” result; with Raiden Shogun, Kujou Sara or Dori in the party the required ER comes out low). The sufficiency check runs on gcsim alone, so only the latest timed particle is used.
er.adjustedResult: This result is a "calculation only" value obtained by the app adjusting the timeline ({{timed}} timed particles added, {{windows}} no-damage periods). It was not checked in gcsim.
er.abyssResultCondition: Conditions of this result: loops {{loops}}, first burst may wait {{first}} s, {{timed}} timed particle entries
er.abyssConditionChanged: The current battle conditions differ from those this result was calculated with. Press Start to calculate again.
er.timingTitle: Check that the Energy Recharge is enough
er.timingNote: Change the Energy Recharge in the table in 1% steps (defaults to the current value); it runs for the chosen number of loops and shows, per character, how many times and how long bursts waited for energy. Start energy is full in normal mode and 0 in Stygian Onslaught mode. You can check without running the ER calculation first.
er.presetsNote: Save the current battle conditions under a name and call them up later (up to {{max}}). Click a name to put it into the fields; saving under the same name overwrites it. Included in the backup.
er.presetLoadTitle: Put these conditions into the fields below
er.presetSummary: Loops {{loops}}, first-burst wait {{first}} s, {{timed}} timed particles, {{enemies}} enemies, {{states}} enemy-state periods
er.presetOverwriteConfirm: "{{name}}" is already saved. Overwrite it with the current conditions?
er.presetFull: You can save up to {{max}} battle conditions. Delete some before saving a new one.
er.presetSaveFailed: Could not save (the storage on this device may be full)
er.enemyParticlesNote: Default is 1 particle every 5–8 s. With 0 particles the calculation runs with no enemy particles.
er.errorVerify: Could not settle the Certain value within the verification limit. Review the party or rotation, or try again.

dps.title: DPS Calc
dps.intro: Runs the current rotation (opening + N loops) in gcsim several times with different seeds and shows the average damage per second (DPS), the spread and a per-character breakdown.
dps.battleShort: In {{count}} of {{runs}} runs the rotation did not last until the end of the battle. Those runs are calculated over the time they lasted.
dps.stateAdjust: Enemy-state correction: {{amount}} ({{percent}}% of the total damage before the correction)
dps.notRunnable: Some elements cannot run in gcsim (resolve them first)
dps.colEnergyWaitsTitle: Average number of times a burst was attempted but waited for lack of energy (per loop = count ÷ (loops − 1); divisor {{laps}})
dps.energyWaitsTotal: Burst energy waits: {{n}} per lap (all characters; count ÷ {{laps}} laps)
dps.energyWaitsNoLap: Burst energy waits: cannot be shown per lap with 1 loop (set loops to 2 or more)
dps.colEnergyWaitSecondsTitle: Average wait per energy wait (from the burst cooldown being ready until the burst goes off; cooldown waits not included). “-” when there was none
dps.energyWaitSecondsTotal: Burst energy waits: {{n}} s per wait on average (all characters; cooldown waits not included)
dps.stats: HP {{hp}} / ATK {{atk}} / DEF {{def}} / EM {{em}} / CRIT {{cr}}·{{cd}} / ER {{er}}
dps.buildNote: Stats are the final values at the start (weapon, artifacts and placeholder values included; buffs during the rotation are not). “Placeholder” is a slot that does not use an owned character’s equipment.
dps.loopsNote: DPS = total damage ÷ time (opening + N loops). Default 5 loops, 1–{{max}}. With few loops the opening has a larger effect.
dps.runsNote: Number of runs with different seeds (default 100, 1–{{max}}). More runs reduce the spread but take longer.
dps.enemiesNote: Up to {{max}} enemies (all at the same position, so AoE hits everyone). Resistance is in % and can be negative. Apply elements to enemies with the rotation’s attacks.
dps.note: Time runs from 0 s to the later of the last action and the last damage. Damage (reactions and extra damage included) is totaled from the detailed log of gcsim {{version}}. Real play differs, for example in enemy movement.
dps.energyNoteOn: A burst without enough energy waits until it builds up (the time is extended). Particles depend on Energy Recharge, skill particles and enemy particles (the default enemy particles are 1 every 5–8 s; 0 means none).
dps.energyNoteOff: Ignores burst energy (the ideal case where bursts can always be used; the same assumption as the app’s time calculation). DPS comes out higher than in actual play.
dps.notRunnableUnknown: The config could not be built (the cause is unknown). Check the party and the rotation.
dps.stale: The party or the rotation has changed. This result is from before the change.
dps.truncated: Of the {{loops}} rotation loops, the shortest run was cut off at loop {{worst}} ({{count}} of {{runs}} runs; the energy may have run short). The DPS covers only what could be executed.

search.title: Auto Rotation Search
search.intro: Builds combinations of on-field order and actions from the roles (attacker / sub-attacker / supporter) of the party members, runs the ones without cooldown violations through gcsim, and ranks them by DPS.
search.rolesTitle: Roles of the party members (click to toggle; used for this search only)
search.rolesHint: Defaults come from the master data roles of each character (or your Database management setting). Rebuilt every time this dialog opens.
search.settingsHint: More runs and more kept candidates make the ranking more accurate but take longer (a few minutes).
search.conditionsHint: The search measures DPS under the same conditions as the DPS calculation (initial + N loops, full starting energy, bursts wait until energy builds up, enemy particles, enemy settings), so results compare directly with a hand-made rotation. While searching, loops are capped at 3 for speed (only the final check uses the chosen number). These settings are shared with the DPS calculation.
search.colParticlesTitle: Energy received from particles before Energy Recharge is applied, averaged per party member per 10 seconds (sum over the party ÷ members ÷ seconds × 10). Includes particle element matching and on-field/off-field differences. At the same DPS, a higher value lets you lower Energy Recharge and put the stats elsewhere.
search.particlesDetail: Average over the evaluated {{seconds}} s: particles generated: {{own}} from skills etc. + {{enemy}} from enemies
search.noMembers: The party has no characters. Build a party first.

modeHint.party: Builds combinations of on-field order and actions from the party members' roles and looks for the highest DPS.
modeHint.current: Starts from the rotation currently on the Gantt chart and changes actions and on-field order one step at a time to find a higher DPS. The knowledge dictionary is not used. The row marked "Current" in the results is your current rotation, for comparison.

search.modeNoCurrent: There are no on-field turns of the party members on the Gantt chart.
search.noCandidates: No candidates could be built (no character has the attacker role, or no usable actions).
search.noValid: No candidate was free of cooldown violations.
search.summary: Of {{candidates}} candidates, {{rejected}} were removed for cooldown violations etc., and {{quick}} were run in gcsim ({{seconds}} s).
search.appliedFirst: Nothing has been placed on the Gantt chart yet. Press "Use this" on the row you want.
search.energyNote: Burst energy shortage is not considered. A party with too little Energy Recharge may not be able to run this in the actual game (check it with "Energy Recharge Calc").
search.energyWaitNoLap: Loops is 1, so per-loop values are unavailable
search.energyWaitTitle: Times a burst was attempted but waited for lack of energy (per loop = count ÷ (loops − 1)) and the average wait per time (from the burst cooldown being ready until it goes off; cooldown waits not included). Same as the DPS calculation
